olivia: Quick question — we're seeing inconsistent behavior when users hit Ctrl+C in the CLI: Node SDK aborts the request immediately, Python SDK sometimes keeps the streaming connection alive for another ~10s. Any ideas on consistent patterns we should recommend?

sam: Yup seen this. Node uses AbortController + fetch semantics, python client uses requests/urllib3 stream which doesn't always interrupt socket read on our cancel path.

olivia: Minimal repro (node):
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal })
  .then(r => r.body.pipeTo(process.stdout));
process.on('SIGINT', () => { ac.abort(); console.log('aborted'); });
```
When I press Ctrl+C it logs "aborted" but the pipe teardown can take a while.

sam: For node, you often need to explicitly destroy the stream reader or call `res.body.cancel()` after abort because underlying socket can be held by stream pipe. Also ensure keepalive isn't set on the agent.

kevin: For python, our client wraps httpx/requests depending on environment. httpx will cancel by closing transport but uvloop + threads can delay. In practice we added a `Client.close()` call on signal to force immediate close. Example: `signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda *_: client.close())`.

olivia: Hmm. Want to propose a cross-SDK guidance: 1) SDKs should expose a cancel/close method; 2) CLI tooling should call that on SIGINT; 3) docs show idiomatic patterns for Node+Python. Sound right?

tasya: Yes. Also add a note about retries/backoff: on abort we should not enqueue retry. Make sure the retry middleware checks `is_aborted` flag before requeue.

sam: Good call. For Node SDK we already have `client.close()` but CLI quickstart still uses raw fetch in examples — we should switch to `await client.stream(...)` so we can call `client.close()` on SIGINT.

kevin: I can open a tiny PR to: a) update CLI example, b) add `SIGINT` handler in examples, c) add small test that simulates SIGINT using process.kill.

olivia: Awesome. Two extra edge-cases: 1) background reconnect/backoff loops (they should stop on abort), 2) long-lived keepalive connections where OS-level TIME_WAIT delays appear. We should call `agent.destroy()` / `transport.close()` where available.

sam: Agree. I'll add a checklist in the SDK README: expose `close()`/`destroy()`; ensure retry middleware respects abort; provide example SIGINT wiring.

devex-bot: New issue created: #4321 "consistent SIGINT + AbortController guidance across SDKs" (assigned: kevin) :sparkles:

kevin: Taking #4321, will draft PR today. tagging @tasya for retry middleware review.

tasya: happy to review — can we also add a tiny e2e that asserts no retry after abort? :+1:

olivia: Thanks all. Let's aim to land before the next release cut. :rocket:
